newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q1 labor costs rose 0.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q1 labor costs rose 0.6 pct.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department employment cost data for U.S. workers in percent changes.
Seasonally adj. 3 months ended: Unadjusted 12 months ended:
Wall Street economists had forecast a 0.9 percent rise in first quarter compensation for U.S. workers.
The Employment Cost Index on March 31 was 131.8 over its 1989 base of 100, compared with 131.0 on December 31.
Labor said that for private industry workers, wages and salaries rose 3.4 percent in the 12 months ended March 1997, versus a 3.2 percent increase in the previous 12 months.

The first quarter rise in wages and salaries was the largest 3-month gain since a 1.0 percent rise in the first quarter of 1996. The first quarter benefit costs rise was the smallest since a 0.1 percent increase in the first quarter of 1996.
